facts.text: Broadly, the period from the ninth century CE till the end of the eighteenth century CE is considered to be the medieval period of Indian history.
facts.quote: Broadly, the period from the ninth century CE till the end of the eighteenth century CE is considered to be the medieval period of Indian history.

facts.text: History gives us a chronological, scientific and systematic account of past events.
facts.quote: History gives us a chronological, scientific and systematic account of past events.

facts.text: Four factors are very important from the viewpoint of history: Individuals, Society, Place and Time.
facts.quote: Four factors are very important from the viewpoint of history. They are - Individuals, Society, Place and Time.

facts.text: History must be based on authentic evidence or proofs, which are known as the sources of history.
facts.quote: History must be based on authentic evidence or proofs. These proofs are known as the sources of history.

facts.text: Sources of history are classified into material sources, written sources and oral sources.
facts.quote: Let us classify these sources into material sources, written sources and oral sources

facts.text: Forts have an important place among material sources; major types are hill forts, forest forts, sea forts and forts on the plains.
facts.quote: Forts have an important place among material sources. Some major types of forts are hill forts, forest forts, sea forts and forts on the plains.

facts.text: Monuments include samadhis, graves and veergala.
facts.quote: Monuments include samadhis, graves, veergala

facts.text: Buildings include palaces, ministerial mansions, Queen's quarters (raniwasa) and houses of common people.
facts.quote: buildings include palaces, ministerial mansions, Queen's quarters (raniwasa) and also houses of common people.

facts.text: Material sources tell us about the development of architecture, economic conditions, quality of art, style of building construction and people's standard of living.
facts.quote: we come to know about the development of architecture, the economic conditions, the quality of art, style of the building construction and people's standard of living in that particular period.

facts.text: Physical sources shown: forts, memorials, buildings, cave sculptures, inscriptions, copper plates and coins.
facts.quote: Physical Sources ... Forts ... Memorials ... Buildings ... Cave Sculptures ... Inscriptions ... Copper Plates ... Coins

facts.text: Since ancient times, coins like kavadi, damadi, dhela, pai, paisa, ana and rupee were used.
facts.quote: Since ancient times, coins like kavadi, damadi, dhela, pai, paisa, ana and rupee were used.

facts.text: Phutaki kavadi means 'the lowest bit of money'.
facts.quote: Here phutaki kavadi means 'the lowest bit of money'.

facts.text: The saying 'Solah ana sach!' means 'Hundred percent true!'
facts.quote: means 'Hundred percent true !'

facts.text: Coins made by rulers using gold, silver and copper tell us about the rulers, their period, governance, religious ideas and personal details.
facts.quote: The coins made by different rulers using metals like gold, silver, copper are important sources of history. From these coins we learn about the rulers, their period, governance, religious ideas, personal details, etc.

facts.text: Coins also show financial transactions, economic conditions and how far metallurgy had advanced.
facts.quote: we also learn about the financial transactions and economic conditions prevailing at that time. We also see how far metallurgy had advanced in that period.

facts.text: Images of Ram-Sita appear on the coins of Emperor Akbar.
facts.quote: From the images of Ram-Sita on the coins of Emperor Akbar

facts.text: Images of Shiva Parvati on the coins of Hyder Ali show the religious co-ordination of those days.
facts.quote: or Shiva Parvati on the coins of Hyder Ali we see the religious co-ordination of those days.

facts.text: The Peshwas used the Arabic or Persian language on their coins.
facts.quote: The Peshwas used the Arabic or Persian language on their coins.

facts.text: An inscription is a carving on a stone or a wall, for example the inscriptions in the Brihadishwara temple premises in Tanjavur.
facts.quote: An inscription is a carving on a stone, or a wall etc. For example, the inscriptions found in the Brihadishwara temple premises in Tanjavur.

facts.text: Many inscriptions of the period of Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Chola and Yadav kings have been found.
facts.quote: Many inscriptions of the period of Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Chola and Yadav kings have been found.

facts.text: An inscription is a very important and reliable source; it helps us understand the language, script and social life of a period.
facts.quote: An inscription is considered to be a very important and reliable source of history. It helps us to understand features like the language, script, social life of a period.

facts.text: Inscriptions carved on sheets of copper are known as copper plates; royal edicts and verdicts are inscribed on them.
facts.quote: Inscriptions carved on sheets of copper are known as 'copper plates'. Royal edicts, verdicts, etc. are inscribed on copper plates.

facts.text: Chaityas, Viharas, temples, churches, mosques, weapons, utensils, ornaments, toys, musical instruments, village boundaries and gates are all material sources.
facts.quote: Chaityas, Viharas, temples, churches, mosques, agiaries, durgahs, mukbaras, gurudwaras, monuments, sculptures, wells, minarets, village boundaries and gates, weapons, utensils, ornaments, clothes, decorative articles, toys, implements, musical instruments are all material sources of history.

facts.text: Written sources include scripts like Devanagari, Arabic, Persian and Modi, bhurjapatras, religious manuscripts, treatises, edicts, decrees, biographies and paintings.
facts.quote: from sources like the writing styles of scripts like, Devanagari, Arabic, Persian, Modi etc. as also from the varieties of different languages, bhurjapatras, religious manuscripts, treatises, edicts, decrees, biographies, paintings, etc.

facts.text: Written sources tell us about food items, attire, conventions, rules of conduct, festivals and people's life.
facts.quote: We can gather information about the food items, attire, conventions and rules of conduct of the people, festivals and about people's life etc. from these sources.

facts.text: Written sources shown: court proceedings, genealogies and Shakavali, correspondence and dispatches, judicial verdicts and orders, treatises and biographies, travelogues of foreign travellers, chronicles and Tavarikh.
facts.quote: Documents of proceedings in the courts of kings ... Geneologies, Shakavali ... Correspondence, Dispatches ... Judicial Verdicts, Orders ... Treatise, Biographies ... Travelogues of foreign travellers ... Chronicles, Tavarikh

facts.text: Travellers from other countries such as Al Biruni, Ibn Batuta and Niccolao Manucci wrote travelogues.
facts.quote: travellers from other countries came to India. They have written travelogues or accounts of their travels. Some of them are Al Biruni, Ibn Batuta, Niccolao Manucci.

facts.text: 'Shrishivbharat' is the Sanskrit biography of Shivaji Maharaj composed by the poet Paramanand.
facts.quote: 'Shrishivbharat' or the Sanskrit biography of Shivaji Maharaj composed by the poet Paramanand

facts.text: Biographies such as Babur's biography and rulers' correspondence help us understand their policies, administrative systems and diplomatic relations.
facts.quote: Babur's biography, 'Shrishivbharat' ... as well as various other biographies of different rulers and their correspondence help us to understand the policies and administrative systems of the rulers and their diplomatic relations with others.

facts.text: Tavarikh or Tarikh means the sequence of events.
facts.quote: Tavarikh or Tarikh means the sequence of events.

facts.text: Tavarikhs written by Al Biruni, Ziauddin Barani, Maulana Ahmed, Yahya Bin Ahmed, Mirza Hyder and Bhimsen Saxena are available.
facts.quote: Tavarikhs written by Al Biruni, Ziauddin Barani, Maulana Ahmed, Yahya Bin Ahmed, Mirza Hyder, Bhimsen Saxena, etc. are available.

facts.text: Bakhar is a type of chronicle that originated in Maharashtra.
facts.quote: Bakhar is a type of chronicle that originated in Maharashtra.

facts.text: Chronicles help us understand political happenings, linguistic transactions, cultural life and social conditions.
facts.quote: Chronicles help in understanding aspects like the contemporary political happenings, linguistic transactions, cultural life, social conditions, etc.

facts.text: Many Marathi chronicles were written many years after the events, so they rely on hearsays.
facts.quote: Many of the chronicles in Marathi were written many years after the events had occurred. As a result, they are seen to rely on hearsays.

facts.text: Some chronicles are Mahikavatichi Bakhar, Sabhasad Bakhar, Chitnisachi Bakhar and Bhausahebachi Bakhar.
facts.quote: Some of these chronicles are Mahikavatichi Bakhar, Sabhasad Bakhar, Chitnisachi Bakhar, Bhausahebachi Bakhar, etc.

facts.text: The works of contemporary western historians Robert Arm, M.C.Sprengel and Grant Duff are also important.
facts.quote: The works of contemporary western historians like Robert Arm, M.C.Sprengel and Grant Duff are also important.

facts.text: Oral sources are folk literature passed on from generation to generation, such as owis, folk songs, powadas, folk tales, legends and myths.
facts.quote: folk literature traditionally passed on from generation to generation. Some examples are - owis, folk songs, powadas, folk tales, legends, and myths. Such type of sources are called 'oral sources' of history.

facts.text: Oral sources shown also include gatha, shlokas, abhangas and proverbs.
facts.quote: Folk songs ... Gatha ... Shlokas ... Abhangas ... Powadas ... Proverbs ... Legends ... Myths

facts.text: Research on history goes on; new sources come to light and history has to be rewritten, so our books and our parents' books differ to a certain extent.
facts.quote: New sources and information come to light through this research. Then history has to be rewritten accordingly. We can see that our history books and those of our parents and grandparents, differ to a certain extent.

facts.text: The Powada of Tanaji was composed by Tulashidas Shahir and portrays the Kondhana campaign.
facts.quote: an extract from a powada composed by Tulashidas Shahir. He portrays the Kondhana campaign in it.

facts.text: The powada contains character sketches of Tanaji, Shelarmama, Shivaji Maharaj and Veermata Jijabai.
facts.quote: The powada contains beautiful character sketches of Tanaji, Shelarmama, Shivaji Maharaj, Veermata Jijabai, etc.

facts.text: Before using sources we must examine their authenticity, see which are genuine and which are fake; their quality is determined with internal standards.
facts.quote: We have to examine their authenticity and see which are genuine and which are fake. Their quality can be determined with the help of internal standards.

facts.text: We study the writers' integrity, personal interests, period and political pressures, and whether they rely on hearsay or give an eyewitness account.
facts.quote: We also have to study the integrity of the writers, their personal interests, the period in which they live and the political pressures on them. It is also important to see whether they rely on hearsay or give an eyewitness account.

facts.text: Information has to be verified with other contemporary sources, as it may be one sided, contradictory or exaggerated.
facts.quote: Their information has to be verified with the help of other contemporary sources. The information may be one sided, contradictory or exaggerated.

facts.text: The author's impartiality and neutrality are very important in writing history.
facts.quote: The author's impartiality and neutrality are very important in writing history.
